title: Likelihood-Ratio Inference for Isotonic Dose Curves with a Single Dose Heap
banked_reason: D0.5 BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: incremental < field; paper_score_ceiling 6.3 < 7.4; salvageable=false; independent validity gate confirmed sound but overframed.
gap_reasons: The contribution remains specific to a single true heap, public treatment distribution and stratum proportions, and positive local slope.

The deterministic calibration enumerates 2^{m^4(2m^5+1)} product points, so it establishes computational existence without delivering a usable inference procedure, making the analyst-facing implementation language excessive.

No executable calibration, transitional coverage study, or numerical comparison is supplied, and the C² parent permits smoother estimators whose precision is not compared with the proposed isotonic interval.

The negative pooled-Gaussian calibration claim does not identify a specific published estimator or workflow (with bibkey and scoped guarantee) that actually applies this pooled-RSS Gaussian cutoff; MaathuisHudgens is described only as regular-discrete Gaussian inference, so the refuted target needs to be made precise or recast as a non-load-bearing diagnostic.
proof_attempt_summary: Four D0 solver rounds developed informal original-record joint tied-group fit/RSS limits and exact uniform asymptotic calibration; the final math review passed and all five cited leaves were attested. The field-floor novelty gate stopped at incremental (score ceiling 6.3 below 7.4), and an independent validity gate confirmed a downgraded stop with re-raise status. F never ran, no Lean theorem is certified, and comparison_target_unspecified remains disclosed; future return needs a genuine re-anchor rather than the same-floor retry.
tldr: A standard programme duration places one true dose heap among continuously varying neighboring durations. On the full supplied smooth parent, the actual count-weighted isotonic fits of learned causal pseudo-outcomes have joint constrained and unconstrained limits that retain one atomic aggregate and distinct continuous and atomic variances. A finite deterministic transitional calibration rule yields a total connected interval with exact uniform asymptotic \(90\%\) causal coverage over every public heap-mass sequence and width \(O_P(\max\{n^{1/3},\sqrt{np_n}\}^{-1})\). Identification is given; the contribution is original-record limit and calibration theory. No finite-row exact coverage or minimax claim is made.
gap: Accessible \cite{Doss2026} v1 Theorems 3.3--3.5 and Appendix C.1--C.2 require a smooth treatment CDF and density. \cite{TangBanerjeeKosorok2012} Theorem 3.7 treats a critical regular lattice. A single shrinking true heap instead supplies one aggregate score with potentially different covariate allocation and effective variance. Neither verified theorem calibrates the actual learned-score paired RSS statistic uniformly through this transition.
fill: The scalar weighted RSS profile reduces the original paired-fit problem to joint invariance and localization of two minimum profiles on random count coordinates. Branch-specific learned-minus-oracle bounds, total normalized pilots, and a deterministic numerical calibration handle feed the uniform coverage and width theorem. A separate atom-only Gaussian comparison prevents confusing valid atom inference with Gaussian calibration of pooled RSS.
